children: Juniper Green Energy on Friday said that it has fully commissioned its 75 MW Tata Hybrid Project in Maharashtra with the operationalisation of the project’s 36.25 MWp DC solar capacity at Bhigwan, Pune.
With this, the entire project comprising 36.25 MWp of solar and 50 MW of wind capacity now stands fully operational, a company statement said.

According to the statement, the project has been developed through Juniper Green Beam Eight Private Limited, a subsidiary of Juniper Green Energy Limited (JGEL), under a 75 MW Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Tata Power.
The solar project is connected at Bhigwan Substation in the Pune district, while the wind component is connected at Nilanga Substation in the Latur district, Maharashtra.
With this commissioning, Tata Power becomes the latest distribution utility to be added to JGEL's growing customer base.
The 50 MW wind component was commissioned in phases during July and August 2026.

Ankush Malik, Whole-time Director and CEO, Juniper Green Energy (JGEL), said, "Completing the project with the commissioning of the Bhigwan solar capacity demonstrates our ability to execute integrated solar and wind projects across multiple locations while maintaining a strong focus on timely delivery." With the commissioning of the Bhigwan solar capacity, Juniper Green Energy’s aggregate operational renewable energy capacity now stands at approximately 2,725 MWp and 503 MWh BESS.
The addition further strengthens the company’s operating portfolio and its capabilities across solar, wind and hybrid renewable energy projects.

Juniper Green Energy is an independent renewable energy producer in India, focused on the development, construction, and operation of utility-scale solar, wind, hybrid, and Firm & Dispatchable Renewable Energy projects.

title: Juniper Green Energy fully commissions 75 MW Tata hybrid project in Maharashtra
